text: macOS icns generation: scripts/gen-icons.sh's icns block was gated purely on `command -v iconutil`, which only exists on macOS — running the script on any Linux dev box or Linux CI runner silently no-ops that block with zero error output, leaving packaging/macos/icon.icns simply absent. Trap: a script that 'looks done' (exits 0, no error) can still have silently skipped its real work when it soft-gates on a platform-only tool. Fix applied: added a Linux-capable fallback (rsvg-convert + a small python3 ICNS-container assembler) alongside the iconutil path, so the script produces a real icon.icns on Linux too. Watch for the same pattern with any other mac-only CLI (plutil, codesign, notarytool, stapler) silently no-op'ing in this Linux-first dev/CI environment for the rest of M3/M4.

cargo-bundle (the CLI used by crates/rylus-server's [package.metadata.bundle]) is not vendored or installed anywhere in this repo/sandbox and cannot be run/tested locally — its manifest schema must be confirmed from its real docs (github.com/burtonageo/cargo-bundle Readme.md), not guessed. Confirmed real mechanism for injecting arbitrary Info.plist keys (e.g. NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription): the `osx_info_plist_exts` key takes a list of file paths whose raw <key>/<value> contents get appended verbatim into the generated Info.plist's <dict> before it closes — those files must NOT be full plist documents (no <?xml?>/<!DOCTYPE>/<plist> wrapper), just bare key/value pairs. Avoids re-deriving this from scratch for the Windows MSI (M4) equivalent research.

scripts/worktree.sh destroy deletes the concern/<tag> branch, not just the worktree directory. Running it before scripts/integrate.sh (instead of after) orphans the worker's commits as dangling objects — recoverable via git fsck --no-reflog + git branch <tag> <sha>, but only if git gc has not run. Always integrate.sh a concern branch to a fast-forward merge FIRST, then destroy its worktree; never destroy-then-integrate. Separately: an uncommitted STATE.md edit sitting unstaged in the main worktree gets silently discarded if integrate.sh's checkout/rebase of a concern branch there fails and its failure handler does git reset --hard — keep STATE.md edits committed, or deferred until after all integrate.sh calls finish, never left unstaged while integrate.sh operates in the same worktree.

Ledger-commit invariant keeps getting violated: ledger.py done --run writes .agents/ledger.jsonl AFTER the concern commit already exists, so the natural flow produces a standalone follow-up commit (see 1c7b773, 6028698, and identically-shaped 33ab4b0/a437b1b on earlier ticks) — exactly the "NEVER a standalone chore(ledger) commit" invariant. Fix: do NOT commit the concern first. Integrate the concern branch, re-run the verify cmd, run ledger.py done --run, and only THEN make ONE commit staging the concern files + .agents/ledger.jsonl + .agents/STATE.md together. Renaming the standalone commit to test(...) does not satisfy the invariant.

integrate.sh checks out BRANCH inside --repo (default: cwd toplevel) before rebasing onto TARGET there. If the concern branch is still checked out in its own worker worktree (not yet removed), the checkout fails outright with 'already used by worktree' — clean failure, no damage. Fix: 'git worktree remove <path>' (NOT worktree.sh destroy, which also deletes the branch) to free the branch before calling integrate.sh; destroy/delete-branch cleanup can happen after, or is moot since the worktree dir is already gone. Separately and worse: if you retry integrate.sh in the main worktree while an unrelated STATE.md edit sits uncommitted there, git checkout of the concern branch can succeed (merging cleanly) but the SUBSEQUENT rebase then fails immediately with 'You have unstaged changes' — because that same STATE.md edit is now sitting on the concern branch's checkout and blocks its own rebase. integrate.sh's failure handler then does 'git reset --hard PRE_REBASE_SHA', silently discarding the STATE.md edit (recorded loss on 2026-08-13, a repeat of the already-known pattern from the prior tick's learning, but via this specific worktree-collision trigger). Net rule: fully vacate/free the concern branch from its worktree AND ensure the main worktree is committed-clean before the first integrate.sh call of a tick, not just 'before integrate.sh runs' in the abstract.

The "NEVER a standalone chore(ledger) commit" invariant is UNSATISFIABLE as written under the mandated worktree flow, and the earlier M3 learning prescribing "do NOT commit the concern first" is WRONG — do not keep re-attempting it. Mechanism: workers must commit their concern files on their own concern/<tag> branch, because that commit is the only thing scripts/integrate.sh has to fast-forward. By the time the supervisor re-runs the verify cmd and calls ledger.py done --run on the integrated tree, the concern files are ALREADY committed (via the ff-merge), so the ledger/STATE write can only ever land as a follow-up commit. Fifth recurrence: 33ab4b0, a437b1b, 1c7b773, 6028698, now 659353f. Renaming it test(...)/chore(...) does not satisfy it. Only two real fixes exist and both need an operator/harness decision, not another worker attempt: (a) the supervisor amends the ff-merged concern commit to also carry ledger.jsonl+STATE.md before pushing, or (b) the invariant is relaxed to permit one trailing ledger/state commit per concern. Stop spending tick budget rediscovering this.

git commit -m '...' -- <path> commits the WORKING TREE copy of that path and silently OVERRIDES a staged deletion. Hit live: 'git rm --cached feed.jsonl' then 'git commit -m ... -- feed.jsonl' re-committed the file (stat showed '3 insertions(+)' on a commit meant to be a deletion) and preflight went CLEAN for the wrong reason - the dirt was committed, not removed. Avoid: commit a staged 'git rm --cached' with NO pathspec, and always read the git commit stat line - a deletion commit must report 'delete mode', not insertions.

A grep-only quality gate can pass against code that is structurally dead. M3G4 (grep notarytool build.yml) exits 0, but every codesign/notarize/DMG step in build.yml is conditioned on secrets.APPLE_DEVELOPER_ID_CERT_P12 != and that secret does not exist on the repo - so CI skips them all and ships an unsigned zip while the gate reports green. WHY IT RECURS: text-presence checks measure that a line was written, never that it can execute. HOW TO AVOID: when a gate greps a CI workflow, also confirm the matched step is reachable - no enclosing if: on an unset secret/var, no non-default input, correct job and ordering - and prefer a gate that asserts the produced artifact (test -f the .dmg from a real run) over one that asserts the source text. Same class of error as the cargo test origin filter that matched 0 tests.

scripts/self-heal-check.sh checks ledger status FIRST and short-circuits with "DONE: <ID> already recorded in ledger — skip rebuild" WITHOUT ever running the --cmd it was given. It therefore cannot detect drift between "recorded done at commit X" and "the verify command fails NOW". Hit live: both M2.P1.S2.T2 (cargo audit) and M2.P3.S1.T2 (npm run a11y) returned that skip message while ledger.py check --rerun was simultaneously RED on those exact todos. Never treat a self-heal-check "already recorded" as evidence the check currently passes — it is evidence only that a row exists. Use ledger.py check --rerun (or run the cmd yourself) to establish current truth.

A provisioning/tooling failure can MASK a real substantive failure of the same check. npm run a11y was failing with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (playwright never npm-installed); fixing only the provisioning made it actually execute and it then failed exit 1 on 2 genuine axe-core violations that had been invisible the whole time. Never record a provisioning fix as closing a todo without re-running the check to a real green. Related: the offending nodes were NOT in any www/ template — scripts/a11y.mjs audits the LIVE DOM after lib.js runs, and ts/utils.ts createOnboardingOverlay() appends a first-run modal straight to document.body (unlandmarked h2/p => axe region; raw accent #00aaff on white => 2.56:1 contrast). Grepping the static templates for the failing selector finds nothing; reproduce a11y.mjs render path and dump document.body.innerHTML instead.
